## What is useful to this repository

The external Round 43 synthesis reports that six blind agents independently converged on its current letter-stream ceiling. Treat that as the external team's reported conclusion, not a verified fact here. Its important operational consequence is that the external team is shifting effort toward physical-page channels that ordinary rune transcriptions omit.

The external image inventory explicitly flags these untranscribed channels:

- Red dot-matrix blocks on p0, p2, p3 (two), p14, p15, p23, p27, p33 (two), p36, p42, p53, p54, p55, and the 2013 0_wisdom artifact. The inventory rates their differing on/off cell patterns HIGH because no symbol for them exists in the rune transcription.
- A low-contrast grey ghost/watermark tree on p55, described as the only non-black-and-red element and rated MED-HIGH as a possible carrier.
- Insect images classified by that inventory as cicadas on p2, p53, p55, and 0_wisdom; a mayfly on p14; and a single wing on p27.
- Bare-branch margin trees on p8/p9 and repeated root-tree margin pairs with dot clusters across p33?, p40, p42, p44, p46, and p49–p54.
- Oversized red drop-cap runes, red-vs-black text, structural section glyphs, and blank-panel/whitespace geometry.

The Round 44 campaign plan places red-ink and p15-grid investigations ahead of a low-priority finite tail that includes a p32/p55 tree cross-mirror diff, cuneiform/5-dot census, and an 86-doublet-site falsifier. This is a useful queue ordering and a warning against duplicating the p55 tree comparison without coordinating.

## Local observation and correction

Inspection of original archive image 72.jpg (LP2 p55) confirms a faint, distinct branching/tree illustration between the text and the repeated insect ornament. Image 49.jpg (p32) has a separate, simpler blurred tree. Endpoint counts from threshold/skeleton experiments on p55 are unstable; no exact branch count is established.

A previous visual guess that the p53/p55 insect was a death's-head hawkmoth is **not established**. The external inventory classifies it as a cicada, which is consistent with the project motif and should be treated as the stronger current lead until the original illustration is source-matched. Do not use ATROPOS/ACHERONTIA as a factual species identification or as an established key.

## How to use this source

Use the external inventory as a checklist and source of research leads, not as authority. Preserve original images separately from any derived dot-matrix/tree annotations. For each candidate channel, require an exact image-coordinate transcription, a source-fixed reading order, and an independent result/control before promoting it. Coordinate with the original-image investigator before running a p55 cross-mirror comparison.
